Fail-closed cannot fire, because a call that is never recognised produces no None to assert on. And each uses `'sov-' + 'witness'`, so the literal never appears in the file and the every-file-that-names-the-witness case cannot see it either.

how_each_survivor_classifies.the four enumeration gaps: All four are resolved by machinery already inside this module. `_agent_names` uses a bespoke one-hop regex where `written_into` exists and is already imported. That is the rule not applied to the enumerator's own name resolution, not a new kind of problem.
how_each_survivor_classifies.the desync: Carried, caused by a withdrawal I recommended, and it too has a fail-closed formulation available.

the_convergence_test_I_set_settled.why_I_am_confident_this_is_not_me_wideni: The test I owe myself is whether a stated rule closes the class rather than the instances. For every survivor here I can write the rule in one sentence, in the same shape as the rule already in the module, and it closes constructions nobody has enumerated - including ones I have not thought of. That was not true in rounds one to three, where each repair listed the escapes it had seen. It is the difference between 'follow bindings through push, destructuring and parameters' and 'refuse what you cannot settle'.
the_convergence_test_I_set_settled.what_would_still_change_this: A defect where refusing would refuse everything - where being right requires understanding what the prompt means rather than what it declares. That is the presence-grading ceiling, which is stated, agreed, and out of this concern's scope. It is the one place where the refactor is genuinely the only answer, and it is already named as such.
